events.event: ABHI Microfinance Bank raised over Rs. 2 billion through the book-building portion of its IPO on the Pakistan Stock Exchange.
events.source_excerpt:
ABHI Microfinance Bank has raised about Rs. 2.05 billion through the book-building portion of its IPO, after demand ran past the shares on offer, according to Pakistan Stock Exchange book-building data and a company announcement.
The book-building tranche covered 99 million of the bank’s 132 million ordinary shares on offer, at a floor price of Rs. 15.00.
PSX data show an indicative strike price of Rs. 15.50, with bids for about 157.17 million shares, which is roughly 159 percent of the offer at the floor and about 106% at the strike.
The company said the book build is Pakistan’s first fintech-led microfinance bank IPO. It reported bids of more than Rs. 2.4 billion, with strong interest from foreign funds, local institutions, and high-net-worth investors.
The remaining 33 million shares will go to the public at the strike price on November 12 and 13, 2026.
ABHI had earlier said the full IPO could raise between Rs. 2 billion and Rs. 3 billion, with proceeds meant to expand its loan book and strengthen its capital base. ProPakistani covered that plan in an earlier report.

events.event: The Pakistani government announced the fifth consecutive reduction in fuel prices, cutting petrol by Rs6.59 and high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 per litre.
events.source_excerpt:
The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices.
Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378.
The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).
The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.
Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.
Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
Rise in fuel prices
The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.
The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.
Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.
On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

events.event: US President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller will become the next White House chief of staff.
events.source_excerpt:
President Donald Trump on Friday announced that Stephen Miller, one of his most powerful and politically aggressive aides, would be his next White House chief of staff following disastrous results for Republicans in the midterm elections.
Miller, whose titles until now were deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, has orchestrated the most polarizing policies of Trump’s second term—most notably a brutal crackdown on immigration that has claimed the lives of US citizens.
Trump made the change public in a statement on his Truth Social platform, writing that Miller would take over from Susie Wiles on Monday—less than a week after Republicans lost the House and Senate in a searing rebuke of Trump’s policy agenda.
In recent days, Trump has privately blamed Wiles for the worst Republican midterm performance in decades, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Wiles submitted her resignation on Thursday, the sources say.
Trump broadly considered three candidates to replace Wiles, the sources say: special envoy Steve Witkoff, director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, and Miller.
But with the looming threat of congressional investigations starting next year, Trump settled on Miller, seemingly because of his zeal in defending the president and his deep loyalty. Miller has been with Trump since his first campaign and stood by him through his political exile in 2021.
Miller had made his interest for the job known inside the West Wing for weeks, ever since Wiles weathered a series of negative stories before the midterms that suggested her job was at risk, the sources say.

events.event: US President Donald Trump is reportedly weighing military options against Iran following midterm elections while opening diplomatic channels through Qatar.
events.source_excerpt:
• US president says world will ‘know very soon’ whether he makes a deal with Tehran or orders strikes
• Calls Qatar’s Sheikh Tamim as Doha steps up its mediation

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is said to be weighing whether to resume large-scale strikes against Iran after Democrats’ sweeping victory in recent midterm elections, even as he opened a new diplomatic channel on Friday by calling Qatar’s emir to discuss efforts to end the eight-month-old conflict.
The call with Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani came amid an intensifying regional diplomatic effort to prevent another round of major hostilities. But Trump has continued to keep military action on the table, saying on Thursday that the world would “know very soon” whether he would make a deal with Tehran or order new strikes to “destroy what is left” of the country.
“I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so,” Trump told reporters, adding that Iran could take 25 years to rebuild from the damage already inflicted.
Friday’s conversation with the Qatari leader focused on diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions. Sheikh Tamim’s office said he had emphasised dialogue and diplomatic means to resolve disputes and prevent further escalation.
Qatar has been playing a key intermediary role in efforts to negotiate an agreement between Washington and Tehran.
Trump’s latest moves illustrate the dilemma confronting him after the Republican party’s midterm debacle. Democrats have won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, giving them an opportunity to challenge his policies during the final two years of his presidency.

- By Shoaib Nizami -
- Nov 07, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has agreed to extend electricity subsidies for protected consumers using up to 200 units per month for another six months, sources said on Saturday.
According to sources, the understanding was reached during negotiations between Pakistan and the IMF last month, following the government’s efforts to provide further relief to consumers on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
Under the proposed arrangement, the subsidy on electricity consumption of up to 200 units, scheduled to end on December 31, 2026, may now remain in place until June 30, 2027.
This means the government could delay the withdrawal of the subsidy to July 1, 2027.
The IMF had previously set a target for ending subsidies on electricity consumption of up to 200 units from January 1, 2027. However, the government reportedly succeeded in securing a six-month extension.

events.event: Pakistan's National CERT has issued an advisory warning banks and critical infrastructure operators about surging AI-powered cyber threats.
events.source_excerpt:
National CERT Warns of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on Banks and Critical Infrastructure
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has warned of growing cyberattacks from artificial intelligence (AI)-powered attacks targeting banks, financial institutions, and critical national infrastructure.
According to the advisory, cybercriminals could use AI technology to automate attacks, identify system vulnerabilities and launch coordinated cyber operations.
The warning highlights the potential risks to the banking sector, particularly core banking systems, digital banking platforms and online payment services.
National CERT Warns of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on Banks and Critical Infrastructure
National CERT has warned that AI-powered cyberattacks could allow attackers to manipulate the account balances displayed to bank customers. Such activities could create confusion and spread panic among customers about the reliability and security of the financial system.
Cybercriminals could also use AI to identify weaknesses in banking networks and exploit them through automated attacks.
The advisory identifies several warning signs that financial institutions should monitor. These include an increase in automated login attempts, unusual financial transactions and suspicious API activity.
National CERT has advised banks and financial institutions to strengthen their security arrangements. It has particularly recommended implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA) and improving the protection of banking systems.
Critical National Infrastructure Also at Risk
The warning also covers essential national infrastructure, including oil and gas facilities, power plants, water supply networks and industrial systems.

events.event: Severe smog has hit central and southern Punjab, with Multan recording an Air Quality Index of 492.
events.source_excerpt:
Bad air quality affects Punjab with beginning of the winter
- By Web Desk -
- Nov 07, 2026
LAHORE: Bad air quality keeps haunting the central and southern parts of Punjab on Saturday as Multan becomes the most polluted city of Pakistan, as per the Air Quality Index (AQI).
Multan’s AQI recorded 492 today, while air quality at Raiwind recorded 316. The AQI at Rahim Yar Khan recorded 304, in Faisalabad 287 and in Lahore 273.
Indian capital city New Delhi ranked first among the most polluted cities of the world with the particulate matter’s level at the Air Quality Index recorded 539 today.
The air pollution and smog haunts Punjab with the onset of the winter. In previous years authorities made desperate efforts to contain smog in cities. The province grappled with severe air pollution, which soared to alarming levels, causing serious public health issues.
For days, Lahore was enveloped by smog, a mix of fog and pollutants, caused by low-grade diesel fumes, smoke from seasonal agricultural burning as temperatures drop with cooling air.
Air pollution level in Lahore once soared to more than 80 times of the level deemed hygienic by the World Health Organization (WHO).
The government closed schools and restricted timing of eateries, other businesses and markets to save general public from the adverse impact of toxic pollution and health problems.

events.event: The Sindh government officially declared Tharparkar a calamity-hit district and ordered emergency measures due to severe drought conditions.
events.source_excerpt:
Published November 07, 2026
KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to officially declare Tharparkar a calamity-hit district amid drought-like conditions across the region.
The decision was taken during a meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, who also directed the authorities to take immediate measures to address the situation in Tharparkar.
The briefing informed the chief minister that all seven talukas of Tharparkar were facing drought-like conditions, with between 85% and 90% of crops either destroyed or rendered unproductive.
According to the briefing, the agriculture extension department estimated crop losses at around 90%, while uneven rainfall had caused crops and natural grass to dry up before reaching maturity.
The chief minister was told that rainfall recorded across Tharparkar's seven talukas in September 2026 ranged from just one millimetre to 36 millimetres.
CM Murad directed the authorities to ensure the provision of drinking water to the people of Tharparkar and ordered the immediate repair and restoration of inactive reverse osmosis plants.
He also directed that all existing sources of water supply be restored without delay.
The chief minister instructed the chief secretary to examine the feasibility of laying a water pipeline from Naukot to Mithi and undertake long-term planning for water supply to the area.
He further sought recommendations on measures that could be taken to support livestock affected by the drought.
CM Murad directed continuous monitoring of relief measures in drought-affected areas, saying the Sindh government would not leave the affected people of Tharparkar alone and would provide every possible assistance.

original_source.name: Geo News
original_source.basis: Official briefing and decision chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.

events.event: Security forces killed four terrorists during an intelligence-based operation in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
events.source_excerpt:
Security forces have killed four India-backed Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during an Intelligence-Based Operation (IBO) in Bannu district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), security sources said on Saturday.
The operation was carried out under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, which aims to eliminate Fitna al-Khawarij and establish lasting peace in the province.
Reports quoted security sources that troops recovered a cache of weapons and ammunition from the terrorists killed during the operation.
Clearance operations are continuing in the area to search for and eliminate any other terrorists who may be present, the sources said.
Pakistan has witnessed a rise in terrorist attacks, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.
The country recorded its highest monthly number of terrorist attacks in 12 years in September 2026.
Islamabad has repeatedly called on Kabul to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan territory to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.
Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban government has failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

It detailed the lawyer’s meeting with Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi on November 2 in Adiala Jail.
“My meeting with Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi was scheduled for 3:30 PM at Adiala Jail on November 2. However, the meeting began at 4:00 PM and lasted for 40 minutes,” the affidavit read.
According to the document, “Bushra Bibi was wearing exceptionally dark sunglasses. When she removed them at the insistence of Imran Khan and myself, she appeared immensely distressed.”
Barrister Safdar stated in the affidavit that “Bushra Bibi informed me she can tolerate neither sunlight nor artificial light.”
“She said she cannot even open her eyes without the glasses,” he added.
Safdar noted in his affidavit: “I observed that her eyesight has been severely affected, while Imran Khan also appeared deeply concerned over her deteriorating condition. Bushra Bibi shared that doctors diagnosed her condition as mature cataracts and informed her that she requires another eye surgery on November 15.”
The counsel added that “Bushra Bibi expressed dissatisfaction with the sanitary conditions in jail as well as her medical treatment, demanding examination and treatment by her private doctors.”
Safdar concluded: “I assured her that I would raise the issue before the court to bring the matter to its official notice.”

events.event: Pakistan won the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championship by defeating South Korea 2-0 in the final in Islamabad.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan have won the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championship, beating South Korea 2-0 in the final in Islamabad.
Noor Zaman and Asim Khan each won comfortably to give the hosts the title.
The win is Pakistan’s 16th gold medal in the tournament’s history and their first since 2016.
Pakistan reached the final with a 2-0 win over Hong Kong China in the semi-final at the Mushaf Squash Complex. Asim beat Wong Chi Him 11-4, 6-11, 11-7, 11-3 in 50 minutes. Noor Zaman beat Lau Tsz Kwan 5-11, 11-5, 11-5, 11-8 in 44 minutes.
South Korea earned their place in the final by beating defending champions Malaysia 2-1. Seojin Oh won the deciding match against Duncan Lee 1-11, 11-6, 11-7, 11-9.
In the women’s event, Pakistan lost 2-1 to Iran. Narges Soltani beat Sehrish Ali 11-9, 11-5, 11-8, and Mahnoor Ali beat Baran Mohammadpoor 11-4, 3-11, 11-8, 11-9 to level the tie. Fereshteh Eghtedar then beat Sana Bahadar 11-8, 11-6, 11-6 to give Iran the win. The result gave Iran’s women their first bronze medal at the championships.
The Asian Squash Federation rescheduled the championship and held it in Islamabad from November 3 to 7. The federation had postponed the event from its original April dates because of rising tensions in the Middle East.
Pakistan will host four more international squash tournaments after the championship, with total prize money of $439,000.

events.event: Pakistani oil refineries face negative refining margins as international petrol prices fell below crude oil prices.
events.source_excerpt:
Pakistan’s oil refineries are facing fresh financial pressure as international petrol prices have fallen below crude oil prices, pushing refining margins into negative territory for the first time in recent history.
According to Topline Research, petrol refining margins dropped to negative $1 per barrel on a seven-day rolling average basis as of November 6. International petrol prices stood at $105.90 per barrel, compared with Dubai crude oil at $106.90 per barrel. On November 5, the daily refining margin fell further to negative $5 per barrel.
The decline became visible in international price data compiled by OGRA and Topline Research. Petrol and Dubai crude prices moved relatively closely throughout much of October before falling sharply towards the end of the month. By November 5, petrol prices had dropped below crude oil prices, putting additional pressure on refinery profitability.
Refining margins, also known as cracks, represent the difference between the selling price of refined petroleum products and the cost of crude oil used to produce them. When petrol prices fall below crude oil prices, refiners face losses on petrol production.
The situation has become more challenging for domestic refineries following the imposition of a Rs. 49 per litre levy on petrol. The combination of negative international refining margins and the additional domestic levy is expected to further squeeze the profitability of Pakistan’s refining sector.
The latest development adds to the financial challenges facing local refineries as international fuel prices and domestic levies continue to affect their operating margins.

original_source.name: TechJuice
original_source.basis: Analysis based on industry data and research reports.

The mission will mark the first joint spaceflight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s manned space program, representing a significant milestone in China-Pakistan space cooperation.
After completing a short-term stay in orbit, the astronaut will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, Gwadar Pro reported on Saturday.

events.event: The Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources declared 27 bottled water brands unsafe for human consumption due to contamination.
events.source_excerpt:
27 bottled water brands declared unsafe for consumption in Pakistan
- By Web Desk -
- Nov 08, 2026
The Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) has declared 27 bottled water brands unsafe for human consumption following tests conducted across the country.
According to the PCRWR, samples of 223 bottled water brands were collected from 20 cities and tested for chemical and microbiological contamination during the July to September 2026 quarter.
The quarterly report found that 195 brands met the required quality standards, while 27 were declared unsafe. Of these, six failed chemical tests and 22 were found to have microbiological contamination.
The brands identified as unsafe include Aab-e-Haram, Imperial Pure Drinking Water, Aab-e-Makran, Water Verse Purified, Gel, Sip, AB Blue Water, HR Water Healthy Life, Sufi, Pure Aqua Tech, Aquafine, Water Time, Al-Suha, Aab-e-Hayat, K&S Aqua Sea, Jairs Safe Life, Athar Premium, Aqua Dor, HHG Sweets and Bakers, Drinkly, One Flo, Premium Safa, Zalmi Pure Mineral Water, New A2Z, Fresh Smart Pure Water and Aqua Indus.
The PCRWR collected water samples from 20 cities, including Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Multan, Karachi, Lahore, Quetta, Faisalabad, Sukkur and Gujranwala.
